headline: TESSERA DATA TOWER BOMBED — 9 DEAD IN CIRCUIT DISTRICT BLAST
body:
A coordinated explosive attack on Tessera Corporation's Relay Tower 7 in The Circuit killed nine people and wounded thirty-four others at 7:22 PM last night, destroying a critical node in Tessera's proprietary data infrastructure and knocking NovaMind BCI service offline for an estimated 600,000 users across the city's eastern grid. The blast, triggered by shaped charges placed on three structural columns at sublevel two, was sophisticated enough that security analysts are ruling out amateur involvement. Tessera's head of security, Admiral Renne Cho-Petrov, called it 'a criminal act of mass terrorism targeting the connected lives of every citizen in Meridian.' Among the dead are six Tessera engineers, two contracted maintenance workers, and one Ferrogate Transit technician present for routine infrastructure work.

A communiqué distributed via pirate broadcast within two hours of the blast claimed responsibility on behalf of a group calling itself the Meridian Liberation Compact, describing Relay Tower 7 as 'a node in the surveillance architecture Tessera uses to monetize and control every thought transmitted across its network.' The message referenced Tessera's controversial 2111 BCI data-harvesting settlement, in which the corponation paid 240 million quanta to resolve allegations of selling unencrypted neural metadata to third parties. Tessera has denied any connection between the settlement and the attack.

The Axiom News Network has confirmed that Tessera is cooperating with Meridian Security Directorate investigators, who have identified at least one person of interest connected to The Collective, a worker cooperative with a history of anti-corporate activism. Collective spokesperson Dara Mensah-Oyelaran issued a statement this morning unequivocally condemning the attack. 'We are not a violent organization. We grieve for the workers who died in that tower.'

Relay Tower 7 served as a major routing hub for the eastern grid's BCI network. Tessera estimates full restoration will take forty-five days, leaving hundreds of thousands of residents with degraded neural interface access — a hardship critics note falls disproportionately on lower-income users who depend on public BCI relays.
aftermath: The Meridian Liberation Compact carried out two more bombings over the following year before Tessera's internal security division, in cooperation with the Graycloaks, identified and captured the cell's leadership — though leaked documents later suggested two of the arrested individuals had no confirmed involvement.
runner_relevance: The bombing created an immediate multi-sided runner market. Tessera contracted extraction teams to recover encrypted hardware from the debris before investigators could fully document it — data retrieval runs paying 5,000-12,000 quanta for intact server components. The Graycloaks quietly auctioned intelligence on the Meridian Liberation Compact's membership to at least three bidders simultaneously, including Tessera security and a Federal Remnant intelligence cell. The BCI blackout in the eastern grid created a surge in demand for human couriers — runners who could operate without compromised neural interfaces commanded premium rates for forty-five days. The Collective, under suspicion, hired protection runners to guard its leadership.
